newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom bill needs a bit more time - deputy.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom bill needs a bit more time - deputy.

text.p: A final draft of Brazil's General Telecommunications Law will not be read in its Chamber of Deputies panel Wednesday as had been previously expected, a congressional official said.
Deputy Alberto Goldman, who is in charge of the bill in its special lower house committee, would probably finish off the bill next week, a press aide said.
"There were lots of proposals for changes put forward at the last minute and the deputy wanted more time to study them with calm," the aide said.

The bill would lay down rules for the privatization of federally owned telecommunications holding Telebras, create a new sector regulator and establish technical rules for telecommunications operators in Brazil.
If approved by the committee, the bill moves to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies. It also needs approval in the Senate.
Communications Minister Sergio Motta has said he expects the bill to be through Congress by the end of June.
